title: Article 362 — Rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 362 required the Union and States to have due regard to covenant guarantees concerning the personal rights, privileges and dignities of Rulers of Indian States. It was omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971 (w.e.f. 28 December 1971), together with Article 291 (privy purses). Article 363A was inserted to provide for cessation of recognition of Rulers and abolition of privy purses.
content.glance: Art 362 omitted by 26th Amendment 1971 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971). Rulers' covenant privileges constitutional guarantee removed; see Article 363A.
content.study:
Article 362 directed constitutional authorities to respect personal rights, privileges and dignities of Rulers as assured under pre-Constitution covenants linked to Article 291 privy-purse arrangements.

Omission: Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971), as part of the same package that omitted Article 291 and inserted Article 363A.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 362 as a living source of enforceable Ruler privileges. Historical analysis should note the 26th Amendment package.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971). Companion provisions: omission of Article 291; insertion of Article 363A; amendment of Article 366(22) definition of Ruler.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Treat Arts 291 and 362 as a paired 26th Amendment omission.
2. Point to Article 363A for cessation of recognition and privy-purse abolition.
3. Do not plead Article 362 as current enforceable privilege.

examples.title: Illustration — Privilege claim after 1971
examples.body: A claim that relies solely on Article 362 for continuance of covenant privileges after 28-12-1971 is misconceived: the article was omitted by the 26th Amendment.

misconceptions.trap: Article 362 still requires due regard to Rulers' privileges.
misconceptions.correction: Article 362 was omitted by the 26th Amendment, 1971. Recognition and privy-purse consequences are governed by Article 363A and ordinary law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 362?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 362 was omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971 (w.e.f. 28-12-1971). It is not living law. See Article 363A regarding cessation of recognition of Rulers and abolition of privy purses.

examTips: Always discuss Art 362 together with Art 291 and Art 363A under the 26th Amendment.
content.migrationNote: Remediated 2026-10-09: accurate 26th Amendment omission. Case-law gate open.

notes: Omission by 26th Amendment w.e.f. 28-12-1971 recorded from standard official sources. No case holdings invented.

keyTakeaways: Paired with Art 291 omission and Art 363A insertion.
